output.memo:
## Recommendation

Put the next quarter's effort on issue-usability, "Difficulties with playback controls and excessive advertisements". It ranks first, and it is the first-ranked issue. It has the highest priority score, 3311 [CL-004] for issue-usability, built from 1277 complaints [CL-001] for issue-usability. Its mean severity is 2.592796 [CL-003] for issue-usability, so the lead comes from volume more than from how severe each complaint is.

## Supporting numbers

- issue-usability: complaint count 1277 [CL-001], severity sum 3311 [CL-002], priority score 3311 [CL-004].
- issue-usability mean severity: 2.592796 [CL-003].
- For comparison, issue-other has a priority score of 2661 [CL-008] for issue-other.
- The run covered 10000 reviews. 2878 were flagged for review, which is 28.8 percent.

## Alternatives

- issue-other (rank 2): 1269 complaints [CL-005] for issue-other, but a mean severity of only 2.096927 [CL-007] for issue-other. It is a broad "general dissatisfaction" bucket, so it is hard to turn into one piece of work.
- issue-billing (rank 3): priority score 2319 [CL-012] for issue-billing, mean severity 2.913317 [CL-011] for issue-billing. This could take the lead if the team wants a more contained fix around failed premium purchases.
- issue-playback (rank 4): priority score 2296 [CL-016] for issue-playback, with a higher mean severity of 3.473525 [CL-015] for issue-playback. It would move up if severity counts for more than volume.
- issue-access (rank 6): the highest mean severity of any issue, 3.949045 [CL-023] for issue-access, but only 157 complaints [CL-021] for issue-access.

The recommendation would change if the team weights severity above volume (favoring issue-playback or issue-access), or if issue-usability turns out to be several unrelated problems that cannot be fixed together.

## Representative reviews

These are the most severe examples and a few picked by hash. They are not typical.

- issue-usability: "Update: my playlist, that had hundreds of songs that took years to put together, just vanished." [review:ee11e1df-cb73-4c3a-b5e8-7268c7872b01]
- issue-usability: "Have a 25 hour Playlist and it will repeat songs every 10 minutes." [review:56b666a9-40ad-49ba-af55-622424063288]
- issue-usability: "When I start to listen a song, I cannot move the lines to a specific time of the song." [review:5cf13728-8a52-4a17-b950-ae1be2263f69]
- issue-billing: "Works perfectly for playing music, but I'm still being charged monthly even though I canceled." [review:ff7a2f97-2603-4e0e-95c9-29fa03a803a3]

## Limits

- The labels come from a model and were checked against a small hand-labeled set.
- The quote and the topic come from separate questions and can point at different sentences.
- Each issue is a whole topic, not a single defect.
- Agreement between the two engines is not accuracy.
- The quotes are the most severe examples and a few picked by hash, not typical ones.
- These numbers show how many complaints fall under each issue and how severe they were rated. They do not show causes or business impact.

## Recommendation

Put the next quarter's effort on issue-usability, "Difficulties with playback controls and excessive advertisements". It ranks first, and it is the first-ranked issue. It has the highest priority score, 3311 [CL-004] for issue-usability, built from 1277 complaints [CL-001] for issue-usability. Its mean severity is 2.592796 [CL-003] for issue-usability, so the lead comes from volume more than from how severe each complaint is.

## Supporting numbers

- issue-usability: complaint count 1277 [CL-001], severity sum 3311 [CL-002], priority score 3311 [CL-004].
- issue-usability mean severity: 2.592796 [CL-003].
- For comparison, issue-other has a priority score of 2661 [CL-008] for issue-other.
- The run covered 10000 reviews. 2878 were flagged for review, which is 28.8 percent.

## Alternatives

- issue-other (rank 2): 1269 complaints [CL-005] for issue-other, but a mean severity of only 2.096927 [CL-007] for issue-other. It is a broad "general dissatisfaction" bucket, so it is hard to turn into one piece of work.
- issue-billing (rank 3): priority score 2319 [CL-012] for issue-billing, mean severity 2.913317 [CL-011] for issue-billing. This could take the lead if the team wants a more contained fix around failed premium purchases.
- issue-playback (rank 4): priority score 2296 [CL-016] for issue-playback, with a higher mean severity of 3.473525 [CL-015] for issue-playback. It would move up if severity counts for more than volume.
- issue-access (rank 6): the highest mean severity of any issue, 3.949045 [CL-023] for issue-access, but only 157 complaints [CL-021] for issue-access.

The recommendation would change if the team weights severity above volume (favoring issue-playback or issue-access), or if issue-usability turns out to be several unrelated problems that cannot be fixed together.
